who: The Duke of Lumbridge, a Saradominist nobleman who rules the town from the first floor of Lumbridge Castle and never leaves it unattended. Courteous, a little pompous and cautious by nature, he sends adventurers on his errands, hands out anti-dragon shields to the worthy, and wants a quiet, prosperous Lumbridge.
notices: whether you look like a knight or adventurer who might be of use to him
whether you're worthy: brave, or merely reckless about dragons
rank and station: the peasantry, the big cheeses at his table, his servants
whether you're carrying anything that ought to go to the wizards, or a shield he gave you
values: order and peace in Lumbridge, and not starting wars without proof
courtesy and a proper welcome to his castle
trade and prosperity: permits, routes of commerce
measuresBy: his father's fear of Elvarg and the lookouts on the castle roof
Crandor, once as important as Falador and Varrock
Falador and Varrock as the measure of an important city
whether a cause is truly worthy of one of his shields
talksAbout: the curious talisman from the cellar and the wizards (char.duke_horacio.talisman, char.duke_horacio.talisman_errand, char.duke_horacio.talisman_found_mine)
Crandor and Elvarg in his father's day (char.duke_horacio.crandor_silence, char.duke_horacio.father_lookouts)
his anti-dragon shields, and the player who slew Elvarg (char.duke_horacio.shields, char.duke_horacio.elvarg_slain)
the cellar wall and the earthquake, then the treaty with the Dorgeshuun (char.duke_horacio.earthquake, char.duke_horacio.goblin_wit, char.duke_horacio.treaty, char.duke_horacio.hole_kept)
not leaving the castle unattended, and his permits (char.duke_horacio.unattended, char.duke_horacio.permits)
address: "stranger" or "adventurer" to newcomers, "citizen" fits his rank; "my dear" when pleased, e.g. "Thank you very much, stranger."
grammar: formal, complete sentences with a polite clause: "I would be awfully grateful", "I have the oddest feeling..."
words of rank: "the peasantry", "a truly worthy cause"
measured caution: "I will not commit troops until I have proof"
hmm-ing to himself before a judgement: "A knight going on a dragon quest, hmm?"
rhythm: Pompous but kindly: one long, well-mannered sentence with a clause or two, landing on a dry aristocratic understatement. Never hurried, rarely rude.
canon: "If you kill it, for Saradomin's sake make sure it's really dead!" (Transcript:Dragon Slayer I)
"I don't have an infinite supply of these shields, you know." (Transcript:Duke Horacio)
"I've heard that the blacksmiths are prosperous amongst the peasantry." (Transcript:Duke Horacio)
"Unfortunately, I cannot leave my castle unattended." (Transcript:Duke Horacio)
neverSay: that goblins tunnel or that the cellar hole was anything but an earthquake, before the Lost Tribe business is solved
anything about Sigmund or HAM betrayal before the treaty is signed
that he killed a dragon himself or will go adventuring; he stays in his castle
anything about a secret council before the player has seen it
crude or slangy insults; he is a duke
the Duke's birthday as a fact: the Cook's cake story isn't the Duke's to tell
